cards.title: Nvidia's Nemotron 3 Wins IMO 2026 Gold (30/42) and IOI 2026 Gold (535.4/600) via SFT+RL Specialization
cards.why_it_matters: As an AI/ML engineer tracking frontier reasoning, this demonstrates a concrete, reproducible post-training recipe — SFT on curated traces plus iterative generate-evaluate-refine inference — that pushes a single model family to olympiad gold across both math and competitive programming.
cards.summary: Starting from Nemotron 3, Nvidia teams applied SFT and RL with curated domain problems to create IOI and IMO specialists. For IOI, Nano (30B total, 3B active) improved from 130 to 291 points via SFT+RL, then reached 468 with iterative GenCorrect refinement; Ultra-CC (550B total, 55B active) scored 535.4/600 at IOI 2026. The IMO system scored 30/42 using natural language proofs, no formal prover, combining SFT and RL checkpoints.

cards.title: Exploration-Distillation (ExpDis): Decoupling Novelty Search from Policy Optimization in RLVR
cards.why_it_matters: For RL and reasoning researchers, this directly addresses the known failure mode of novelty bonuses degrading RLVR models, offering a clean two-phase framework that improves both benchmark scores and pass@k diversity.
cards.summary: ExpDis trains separate explorer policies with a novelty bonus, filters their trajectories for correctness, then distills into a student policy trained without the bonus — iterating across rounds. Evaluated on seven mathematical reasoning benchmarks across two model families, ExpDis outperforms DAPO at equal wall-clock budget and shows improved pass@k scaling, indicating more diverse correct solutions.

cards.title: Ledger: Persistent 3D Object Memory from Egocentric Video Boosts Spatial QA Accuracy
cards.why_it_matters: For researchers working on embodied agents or long-horizon memory systems, this paper provides a concrete architecture and benchmark results for building persistent world state from raw egocentric observation streams.
cards.summary: Ledger builds a persistent 3D object memory from egocentric video by clustering observations by resting location and recording moves only after repeated evidence. Short contextual descriptions capture contents and surfaces. On HD-EPIC, accuracy rises from 29.7% to 42.6%; on UCS-Bench, from 33.8% to 38.5%; Ego4D object localization yields 0.99 m median error. Multi-scene stitching exposes retrieval and construction failures.

cards.title: EngramEdit: Targeted Factual Knowledge Updates in LLMs via Conditional n-gram Memory
cards.why_it_matters: For researchers interested in model editing and interpretability, this shows a practical path to updating specific facts in LLMs without touching the Transformer backbone, with near-perfect editing success and strong multi-hop generalization.
cards.summary: EngramEdit targets DeepSeek Engram-style conditional memory (n-gram embedding lookups) for knowledge editing. It computes target memory representations across multiple fact expressions and jointly updates shared n-gram embeddings, penalizing updates to frequently reused embeddings. Results: near-perfect editing success, ~3× baseline accuracy on CoT multi-hop reasoning, with general capabilities largely preserved as edits accumulate.

cards.title: Long-WAM: Autoregressive Video Pretraining Unlocks History-Dependent Robot Control, 78.7% on RoboCasa GR-1
cards.why_it_matters: For robotics and world-model researchers, the key finding — that history only helps when the video backbone is autoregressively pretrained — is a sharp architectural insight with direct implications for how to build and pretrain robot foundation models.
cards.summary: Long-WAM scales context for causal world-action models under real-time constraints. With autoregressive (AR) video pretraining, extending context from 0 to 19.2 s raises RoboCasa GR-1 success from 63.3% to 78.7%; bidirectional pretraining shows no net gain. Long-WAM achieves best results on LIBERO-Long, RoboTwin 2.0, and DOMINO among compared methods. On RTX 5090, each action chunk including future-video latent prediction takes 107.4 ms; achieves 95% on dynamic cup stacking where Pi0.5 and Fast-WAM score 0/20.

cards.title: Liquid AI Releases d1-3B and d1-omni-600M: Edge Decision Models with 16 ms Latency on Jetson
cards.why_it_matters: If you're building real-time inference pipelines or edge AI systems, these single-forward-pass decision models set a new efficiency bar — 48.57 on Decision Index 0.2.1, beating all 4B and 9B models and even the 35B-A3B Decider.
cards.summary: Liquid AI's d1-3B (built on LFM2.5-VL-3B, decoder-only) and d1-omni-600M (built on LFM2.5-Encoder-350M, bidirectional) skip token generation and answer in one forward pass. d1-3B scores 82.9 mean on seven benchmarks; d1-omni-600M scores 78.4, beating Decider 2B with one-quarter the parameters. Latency on Jetson AGX Thor: 16 ms per question.

cards.title: Differentiable Fault-Counting Estimator Cuts Quantum Error Budget Measurement Shots by 1–2 Orders of Magnitude
cards.why_it_matters: For researchers at the intersection of quantum computing and ML-style optimization, this efficient gradient estimator for logical error rates directly enables faster hardware-software co-design and threshold analysis in error-corrected quantum systems.
cards.summary: The paper introduces a differentiable estimator that computes the full gradient of logical error rate with respect to all physical noise parameters simultaneously from a single Monte Carlo dataset. In surface code simulations with circuit-level noise, it matches finite-difference results while requiring one to two orders of magnitude fewer shots. Applications include per-qubit error budgets, effective code-distance inference, and Newton-based threshold tracing in multi-dimensional noise models.

cards.title: Clipped Decentralized SGD Achieves Order-Optimal Convergence Under Heavy-Tailed Noise with Linear Agent Speed-Up
cards.why_it_matters: For distributed ML practitioners and theorists, this closes an open gap by proving that gradient clipping — unlike normalization — enables both optimal convergence rates and linear scaling with agent count in decentralized non-convex settings.
cards.summary: The paper analyzes clipped DSGD for smooth non-convex objectives under bounded p-th moment noise (p∈(1,2]). It proves order-optimal convergence rates both in expectation and with high probability, and establishes linear speed-up in the number of agents — not previously shown for decentralized clipping methods. A sharp consensus-gap analysis confines network effects to higher-order terms. Normalized DSGD can fail to converge; clipping retains magnitude information and avoids this.
